news.full_article_text: Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says - Published 14 November 2026, 03:10 GMT An upgrade to a decades-old telecoms network in the US caused the longest nationwide grounding of flights since the 11 September 2001 attacks. Friday's stoppage occurred when part of a key system that allows air traffic controllers and pilots to communicate was switched to fibre from copper wiring so old it has been discontinued, said US Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy on Saturday. US planes were grounded for more than four hours, affecting thousands of flights and passengers. Earlier Homeland Security Secretary Markwayne Mullin said there was no indication of a cyber-attack and that everybody was safe. Here's what we know. What caused the stoppage? On Friday afternoon, a government contractor called L3Harris was continuing work on upgrading an aviation telecoms network. As it swapped out copper lines for fibre at a remote location in the US, L3Harris installed a router - a piece of equipment which basically directs traffic across the network. According to Duffy, that router started flooding others in the air traffic control system, sending 1,000 connection attempts every four to five seconds. As a result, 17 out of 22 air route traffic control centres in the US experienced "instability" on voice and ground communications, said Bryan Bedford, administrator of the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA). It took the aviation authority 45 minutes to identify where the problem was because maintenance is logged manually on paper. This meant the FAA had to "pore through" the physical documents "to figure out who's working on what", Bedford admitted. As a precaution as it tried to track down the cause, Bedford said the decision was made to ground all flights. Aviation analyst Miles O'Brien described the US system as "a house that's about to be condemned". He told the BBC: "I think most of us could look at this and go 'this is a system in the United States that we have allowed to decay'. It is worse than a fixer-upper." Duffy said the system needed a complete overhaul, estimating a $50bn price tag. In the meantime, he said authorities would work to determine whether it was "incompetence" or faulty equipment that led to the outage. He also said there would be "re-evaluation" of allowing upgrades to be done during the day. In a statement on Saturday afternoon, L3Harris confirmed it was working with the FAA to modernise the airspace communications infrastructure and said it was supporting the agency with its investigation. "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travelers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously," the firm said. Juliette Kayyem, US assistant secretary of Homeland Security under President Barack Obama, questioned why an upgrade was done on one of the week's busiest days for travel. "You don't do it on a Friday when there's lots of air traffic controllers," she said "You try to find ways to minimise its upgrade so you're not maybe doing it across the board in a single moment but you also have to have systems that are ready to step in if the upgrade in any way begins to threaten the system," Kayyem added. A spokesperson for L3Harris said is it "supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel". He added: "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously." How many flights were affected? The ground stop led to more than 8,500 delayed and nearly 8,000 cancelled flights on Friday, according to FlightAware. The FAA's initial announcement at 15:54 EST (20:54 GMT) said all flights departing within the US would be grounded until further notice. More than 3,500 airplanes were in the air at the time. Some were diverted to other airports and others flew on to their destinations. Hours later, some flights were allowed to take off from San Francisco International airport. The FAA opened skies again at 20:15 EST. - Have you been affected by the flight disruption? Get in touch 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop What about international flights? All US-bound air traffic from Eurocontrol member states was suspended. There are 42 Eurocontrol member states, including dozens of EU nations, the UK and Turkey, as well as Israel and Morocco. Passengers travelling from the UK have been warned of possible disruption on Saturday morning. A number of flights to the US from Heathrow airport were cancelled and delayed, but Manchester airport said no significant disruption was expected. Flights were operating as normal from Gatwick airport. Australia's largest international airport, Sydney, had grounded all US-bound flights, but scheduled flights are now expected to depart as planned. Air Canada also cancelled flights between the US and Canada. When will normal service resume? Duffy said on Saturday: "We are back at full operations." But, as he predicted on Friday, it is taking time to unwind what happened. FlightAware said more than 3,500 flights in the US were cancelled while 2,000 were delayed. Delta Air Lines and United Airlines said they were resuming operations but they both cancelled 20% of their flights on Saturday. American Airlines cancelled 520 journeys. Meanwhile, JetBlue cancelled 40% of its scheduled journeys. Luggage from cancelled flights at Ronald Reagan airport What are your rights? In the US, UK and the EU, airlines may be liable for compensation if the reason for a delay is deemed within their control, such as a fault with the plane or pilot sickness. As such, airlines do not have to provide compensation to passengers for air traffic control problems. But passengers are still protected to a certain degree under US federal - and country-specific - laws. Under the FAA Reauthorization Act of 2024, cancelled or "significantly delayed flights" - defined as three hours for domestic flights and six hours for international routes - must be offered alternative travel or a full refund of the fare if the passenger chooses not to fly. It also requires all air carriers to issue refunds for tickets purchased with credit cards within seven business days of the request, and 20 days for tickets purchased with another form of payment. Passengers accepting a new flight cannot receive a refund. In the US, there is no requirement for airlines to provide meal vouchers or accommodation, but some may offer complimentary support to customers. However, if passengers are travelling from the UK to the US or flying with a UK carrier, you may have additional rights. news.headline: 'Miracle on Mississippi' - All passengers rescued after New Orleans cruise ship collision
news.story_lead: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans - Published 13 November 2026 Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for.
news.full_article_text: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans - Published 13 November 2026 Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. - Were you in the area at the time of incident? Get in touch . There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority. Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side, Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort. The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway. On Saturday, Moreno said that nine people are still in hospital. She said that the captain of the ship was injured in the accident but refused medical treatment until he knew all passengers and crew were accounted for. US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue had been an "incredible job". Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what had occurred. Still covered in dirt from the boat crash, Joe Knab of Kansas told New Orleans NBC affiliate WDSU that the ship quickly capsized after the collision. He spent about 20 minutes in the water before being rescued. "When we first went in we were bobbing underneath the water; it was sinking pretty fast, but we finally got out of there," he said. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he had seen the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he had seen passengers and crew "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. Built in 2015, the vessel has at least four decks. Get in touch If you were in the area at the time of the incident, please get in touch. Related topics

hindi_translation.full_article_text: Watch: Cruise ship seen sinking after collision with cargo ship in New Orleans - Published 13 November 2026 Some 130 people on a cruise ship docked in New Orleans have been rescued after it was struck by a tanker. The cruise ship, American Heritage, was left lying on its side in the Mississippi River after it was hit by the cargo vessel Atlantic Asphalt. The collision left 32 people from the stricken riverboat in hospital with non-critical injuries, but no-one unaccounted for. Officials hailed it as a "miracle on the Mississippi". The exact cause of the crash remains under investigation, but US Coast Guard Capt Melanie Burnham said: "There seems to be some type of a loss of steering." New Orleans Mayor Helena Moreno told a news conference on Friday that all credit in the rescue effort should go to first responders who "literally jumped right in to help". "We have zero people unaccounted for, which truly is a miracle on the Mississippi," Moreno said. Calls about the collision began around 13:30 EST (18:30 GMT) on Friday, when people began trying to help passengers escape the boat as it took on water, Port of New Orleans chief Melanie Montroll told the news conference. - Were you in the area at the time of incident? Get in touch . There were about 129 passengers, in addition to crew members, on the American Heritage at the time of the collision, according to the port authority. Passengers began getting off the paddlewheeler vessel, operated by American Cruise Lines, as it started listing before tipping onto its side, Moreno said. Tugboat operators, police and other rescuers rushed to help while officials shut down traffic in the Mississippi River during the rescue effort. The American Heritage had been finishing an eight-day cruise calling at destinations in Louisiana and Mississippi along the waterway. On Saturday, Moreno said that nine people are still in hospital. She said that the captain of the ship was injured in the accident but refused medical treatment until he knew all passengers and crew were accounted for. US President Donald Trump posted on Truth Social that the rescue had been an "incredible job". Governor Jeff Landry also hailed the rescue as a "miracle on the Mississippi" given the "sheer number of people who were on that cruise ship" who were rescued. Ships have operated safely on the Mississippi River for years, Landry said, pledging to investigate what had occurred. Still covered in dirt from the boat crash, Joe Knab of Kansas told New Orleans NBC affiliate WDSU that the ship quickly capsized after the collision. He spent about 20 minutes in the water before being rescued. "When we first went in we were bobbing underneath the water; it was sinking pretty fast, but we finally got out of there," he said. Jamie Holford, a witness to the crash, told the BBC's US partner CBS that he had seen the cruise ship hit the dock following the collision. "It sounded like a war movie. Just imagine tons of steel crunching. That's what it sounded like," he said. "It looked like something off the Titanic." Holford added that he had seen passengers and crew "hollering" and "crying" as they tried to get off the ship while it was sinking. The American Heritage can carry up to 150 guests and features a glass-enclosed restaurant, fitness centre and three guest lounges, according to its website. news.headline: US has floated Ukraine ceding Donbas for Nato membership, Zelensky says
news.story_lead: - Published 14 November 2026, 10:30 GMT US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, and a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties". The Ukrainian leader's comments came after US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine.
news.full_article_text: - Published 14 November 2026, 10:30 GMT US negotiators have touted the idea of Ukraine withdrawing its remaining forces from the eastern Donbas region in exchange for Nato membership, President Volodymyr Zelensky has said. The US has not confirmed Zelensky's comments, and a US official told the BBC "many ideas continue to be discussed but any final deal will have to be agreed to by both parties". The Ukrainian leader's comments came after US envoys met Russian President Vladimir Putin and Zelensky as part of US efforts to end the war between Russia and Ukraine. Kyiv has long sought membership of the military alliance, but this has previously been opposed by the US and others while Russia has said another Nato member on its border is unacceptable. Russia launched a full-scale invasion of Ukraine in February 2022. It controls most of the industrial region of Donbas and Zelensky has consistently said Ukraine is unwilling to give up sovereign territory. "The Americans raised a question: 'What if Ukraine joins Nato? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?' This was the first time this had been raised," Zelensky said in remarks released by his office on Saturday. He went on to say that if he received a specific proposal that contained security guarantees, no constraints on Ukraine's military and funds to rebuild the country, he would put it to a referendum. US envoys Jared Kushner and Steve Witkoff travelled to the Irish capital, Dublin, on Thursday to meet Zelensky, after a round of talks with Putin in Moscow. Comments by both Putin and Kremlin officials suggest that Russia's position on the war has not shifted. It has previously proposed limits on the size of Ukraine's military, territorial concessions and Kyiv's guaranteed neutrality as conditions of a peace deal. Ukraine has rejected these, arguing that such constraints would hamper its ability to stave off any future invasion. Other Nato members apart from the US are wary of membership for Ukraine - and it is understood that Ukraine itself sees that as unrealistic. The Kremlin has always been fiercely opposed, too. It is one reason why Russia started this war in the first place. It is possible the American envoys were exploring Ukraine's "red lines" when it comes to occupied land in the Donbas. Zelensky said recently that the US mediators believed Kyiv only had to cede territory to achieve peace and were applying pressure, keen to do a deal as soon as possible. Ukraine is sure that Russia's ambitions are far greater and has long seen Nato as its only sure protection. So it is also possible that Zelensky made this suggestion public in order to re-open a discussion that had been considered all-but closed. He maintains that the idea is now "back on the agenda" as part of an "extremely difficult conversation" on European security. It also looks like Ukrainian push-back against Russia's renewed hardline stance. Moscow now talks about a "new European security architecture", which is long-standing Russian code for a weaker Nato. The issue appears to have been the main focus at the latest round of talks between Ukraine, Russia and the US in Abu Dhabi this week. Hours after Zelensky's remarks, Jared Kushner appeared keen to dampen down any US offer of Nato membership for Ukraine, urging "confidentiality" in a sensitive process. He said that "maximalist" proposals had been reported from the negotiations, along with "strong political rhetoric". In what read like a reproach to Kyiv, Kushner referred to "private discussions" aimed at exploring new ideas about ending what he called a "horrible war". He said the hope was that those ideas might lead to new proposals or breakthroughs. Russia currently occupies roughly a fifth of Ukrainian territory, including most of the Donetsk and Luhansk regions that compose the Donbas. It has insisted again that it will not agree to a ceasefire until a final peace deal is in place that would include Ukraine ceding control of those parts of the Donbas Russian troops have not captured, in addition to the Crimean peninsula Moscow annexed illegally in 2014. The latest round of talks come after a period of fraught relations between Kyiv and Washington over Ukrainian strikes on oil facilities deep inside Russia, which Trump had asked Ukraine to pause to facilitate the supply of Russian diesel to ease global fuel prices. Zelensky then accused US officials of limiting Ukraine's Starlink internet service , which it uses to co-ordinate defensive operations, while Trump said it was "time for Ukraine to get a new president" and called for fresh elections. Elections are suspended while Ukraine remains under martial law, but Zelensky has previously said he was willing to hold them within months of a peace deal being reached and would give up the presidency in exchange for Nato membership. The company had hoped to catch both the bottom and upper stages of the rocket using mechanical arms - nicknamed chopsticks - on its launch tower.

news.headline: Copper wire upgrade caused nationwide flight suspension, US transport secretary says
news.story_lead: Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says - Published 14 November 2026, 08:42 GMT A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said. Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment. The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said.
news.full_article_text: Watch: US ground stop caused by issue during copper wire update, transport secretary says - Published 14 November 2026, 08:42 GMT A nationwide US ground stop that caused thousands of flight cancellations was caused by an issue following a copper wire upgrade, Transport Secretary Sean Duffy said. Duffy told a news conference that the government was trying to find out whether the problem was caused by "incompetence" on the part of the company doing the upgrades, or faulty equipment. The US government does not believe it was as a result of a cyber-attack, although an investigation is still under way, Duffy said. Friday's suspension was the longest such incident since the 11 September 2001 attacks on the US and the disruption is expected to last for days. Maintenance was being carried out to switch from copper wire to fibre by a contractor called L3Harris, a technology provider company, Duffy said. The US has "an incredibly old telecommunications system", he added. "It was such an old wire that it was being discontinued," he said. The transport secretary explained that a router that was being worked on had started flooding other air traffic control systems and created communication issues with planes which led the government to shut down the airspace for safety reasons. Bryan Bedford, who heads the Federal Aviation Administration (FAA), told the same news conference: "We see zero evidence of anything nefarious, and zero evidence of anything AI related." On Saturday L3Harris said it had completed over 70% of the work to modernise communications infrastructure before the shutdown. "We are supporting the FAA in its investigation to understand the conditions that led to the 13 November ground stop of our nation's air travel," it said in a statement. "L3Harris takes the nationwide ground stop and its impact on travellers, airlines and air traffic operations seriously." 'We'll get home one day' - US travellers impacted by nationwide ground stop No flights were allowed to take off from the continental US for more than four hours from 15:54 EST (19:54 GMT) on Friday. More than 3,500 flights were cancelled and more than 2,000 delayed in the US on Saturday, according to tracking website Flight Aware, as knock-on disruption continues. In some cases, passengers were left stuck inside planes on the tarmac, unable to take off or to return to the gates. Some international flights were allowed to depart US airports, in an apparent effort to clear space. Duffy warned that a similar issue could arise again unless the US Congress approved upgrades to air traffic control infrastructure. US President Donald Trump has requested $30.1bn for the upgrades. Both chambers of Congress are currently controlled by the Republican Party. Former TSA Administrator John Pistole told the BBC that "the fact that they were able to get it restarted in four-and-a-half hours is good news - it shows a resilience in the system - but what's to say it's not going to happen tomorrow?" A nationwide ground stop has only been ordered one other time since all flights were banned from take-off for several days following the 11 September 2001 attacks. news.headline: Akhilesh Yadav Reveals Congress Demanded 181 Seats Amid Major Uttar Pradesh Policy and Governance Updates
news.story_lead: Samajwadi Party chief Akhilesh Yadav publicly revealed for the first time that the Congress party had requested 181 seats during political negotiations. The announcement coincides with several administrative, developmental, and governance initiatives in Uttar Pradesh, including an evaluation of the state's smartphone scheme and upcoming census activities.
news.full_article_text:
### Seat Negotiations and Major Governance Developments in Uttar Pradesh

In a significant political disclosure, Samajwadi Party (SP) chief Akhilesh Yadav revealed that the Congress party had requested 181 seats during seat-sharing discussions. This marks the first public confirmation of the specific number of seats sought by Congress in coalition talks.

### Key Policy, Evaluation, and Election Administrative Updates

- **Impact of Smartphone & Tablet Scheme**: A study conducted by the Indian Institute of Management Lucknow (IIM-L) revealed that the Uttar Pradesh government's free smartphone and tablet distribution scheme has successfully benefited 3 crore (30 million) individuals across the state.
- **Homeless Count under Census 2027**: As part of the preliminary operations for Census 2027, Uttar Pradesh authorities will conduct a targeted headcount of homeless individuals on the night of January 4.
- **EVM Demonstration Centers**: To enhance voter awareness, Electronic Voting Machine (EVM) demonstration centers are scheduled to open across all districts of Uttar Pradesh starting November 20.
- **Voter Roll Accuracy**: Administrative strictness has been announced regarding electoral roll updating; Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and officials may face deduction or forfeiture of their honorarium if voter rolls contain errors.
- **Skill Development Focus**: Prime Minister Narendra Modi is scheduled to address and spotlight skill development programs during a major event in Lucknow on November 21.
- **Regulatory Actions**: State authorities have initiated enforcement drives, taking action against 20 pollution testing centers for violating operational norms, while also seeking strict regulatory restrictions on the illicit diversion of codeine-based cough syrups.
bullet_points: Samajwadi Party leader Akhilesh Yadav disclosed that the Congress party demanded 181 seats during negotiations.
An IIM Lucknow study assessed that Uttar Pradesh's free smartphone and tablet distribution initiative reached 3 crore beneficiaries.
Uttar Pradesh will conduct a specialized count of homeless citizens on the night of January 4 as part of Census 2027 preparations.
EVM demonstration centers are set to open state-wide in UP from November 20 to familiarize voters with voting procedures.
Errors in voter registration rolls may lead to loss of honorarium for Booth Level Officers (BLOs) and concerned administrative officials.
Prime Minister Narendra Modi will highlight national skill development initiatives at a Lucknow event on November 21.
Enforcement drives led to action against 20 non-compliant pollution testing centers in Uttar Pradesh.
UP state agencies are pushing for stringent controls to curb the illegal diversion of codeine cough syrups.

Start date for EVM demonstration centers in UP: November 20.

- **Digital Inclusion Initiatives**: The assessment of UP's smartphone scheme by IIM Lucknow demonstrating 3 crore beneficiaries serves as a case study for evaluating technology-driven social welfare schemes.

hindi_translation.full_article_text:
### उत्तर प्रदेश में सीट बंटवारे और प्रमुख प्रशासनिक अपडेट

एक महत्वपूर्ण राजनीतिक खुलासे में, समाजवादी पार्टी (सपा) प्रमुख अखिलेश यादव ने बताया कि कांग्रेस पार्टी ने गठबंधन वार्ता के दौरान 181 सीटों की मांग की थी। यह पहला मौका है जब कांग्रेस द्वारा मांगी गई सीटों की संख्या की आधिकारिक पुष्टि हुई है।

### प्रमुख नीतिगत, मूल्यांकन और निर्वाचन प्रशासनिक अपडेट

- **स्मार्टफोन और टैबलेट योजना का प्रभाव**: भारतीय प्रबंध संस्थान लखनऊ (IIM-L) के एक अध्ययन से पता चला है कि उत्तर प्रदेश सरकार की मुफ्त स्मार्टफोन और टैबलेट वितरण योजना से राज्य भर में 3 करोड़ लोगों को लाभ हुआ है।
- **जनगणना 2027 के तहत बेघरों की गिनती**: जनगणना 2027 की शुरुआती तैयारियों के तहत, उत्तर प्रदेश प्रशासन 4 जनवरी की रात को बेघर लोगों की विशेष गिनती करेगा।
- **ईवीएम प्रदर्शन केंद्र**: मतदाताओं को जागरूक करने के लिए 20 नवंबर से उत्तर प्रदेश के सभी जिलों में इलेक्ट्रॉनिक वोटिंग मशीन (EVM) प्रदर्शन केंद्र खोले जाएंगे।
- **मतदाता सूची की शुद्धता**: मतदाता सूची के नवीनीकरण में त्रुटियों को लेकर कड़ा रुख अपनाया गया है; मतदाता सूची में गड़बड़ी पाए जाने पर बूथ लेवल अधिकारियों (BLO) और संबंधित अधिकारियों का मानदेय रोका जा सकता है।
- **कौशल विकास पर जोर**: प्रधानमंत्री नरेंद्र मोदी 21 नवंबर को लखनऊ में आयोजित एक कार्यक्रम के दौरान कौशल विकास पहलों पर विशेष ध्यान केंद्रित करेंगे।
- **नियामक कार्रवाई**: मानक का उल्लंघन करने पर उत्तर प्रदेश में 20 प्रदूषण जांच केंद्रों पर कार्रवाई की गई है, जबकि कोडीन युक्त कफ सिरप के अवैध इस्तेमाल पर सख्त पाबंदी लगाने की मांग की गई है।

The case has been a subject of significant legal and diplomatic attention between India and the United States. Gupta's submission aims to present his defense directly to the court as legal proceedings continue.
